context:
Goal: the fastest outcome without losing accuracy.
Problem (goal): prose-only steps could all land first as one wave, or run beside code. Today one batch merges at a time, so a prose batch waits behind a running code batch.
Based on (read): a prose PR already gets one short two-check review round. A lone batch CI run takes 33-38 minutes (5 runs, plan 3.4).
Based on (measured): tonight the plan copy, one prose file, failed that short round twice on real errors: a misquote of you, a false claim about the project-ops script, and your pick c described as fitting your shared-tool ruling (2026-11-11).
Departs from: plan 3.13, where an express pass skips the review when the quotes match the log — adds prose batches that go next in the merge order.
Meanwhile: the retrospective waits on this item only.
holds: When prose-only steps merge relative to code, and whether prose keeps its one short review round.

options.gain: Prose waits at most one running batch, and the wait ends for everything once lanes merge on their own green.
options.how: Until lanes merge on their own green (R42 part 2), a ready prose batch goes next in the merge order, ahead of a ready code batch. Prose keeps the one short round; the skip applies only to a PR of verbatim quotes and their times. R42 part 2's planning starts in the first hour of the fan-out.
options.label: Prose goes next in line (Recommended)
options.lose: A ready code batch can wait one prose run.

options.how: Every prose step lands first, and code waits for the prose wave.
options.label: All prose first
options.lose: Code lanes sit idle for the prose wave.

options.how: Plan 3.13 as written: prose skips the review round when its quotes match the log.
options.label: Skip review when quotes match
options.lose: Tonight's three errors would have merged, since none was in a quote.

reply: Answered in the retrospective's chat at 20:24 CST: "yes — i figure some prose has to wait behind some code changes otherwise it'd be confusing, but for a large part prose truly can all be done first — u can even work on readying that now!" Reading: a, moved toward b. Prose-only steps go first, as their own batches, ahead of code. A prose step that describes code not yet on main waits behind that code. The one short round stays. The quote-match skip applies only to a PR of verbatim quotes and their times. The retrospective is sorting every open step into prose, prose-after-code and code now. Home: decision docs-only-prs-skip-review.
title: Should prose-only steps jump ahead of code?
why: You asked at 20:10 and 20:13 CST whether prose should go first as an express round (measured 2026-11-11, #2605 failed its prose round twice tonight).
